purpose: Restore the factory camcorder profile selection so the platform exposes the 4K, 8K, DCI and high-speed video profiles that the Xiaomi camera application lists for its resolution and frame-rate controls.

stock_evidence.media_profiles_vendor_xml: absent on the factory vendor image and on the phone; the loader treats the key as a /vendor/etc marker and upgrades to the codec-variant table

loader.semantics: With media.settings.xml unset, getXmlPaths() searches product, odm, vendor and system for media_profiles<ro.media.xml_variant.profiles>.xml, defaulting to _V1_0. With media.settings.xml set to a /vendor/etc path, the QTI branch replaces it by /vendor/etc/media_profiles<ro.media.xml_variant.codecs>.xml when that file exists.
loader.codec_variant_source: /vendor/etc/init/init.qti.media.rc copies vendor.media.target_variant into ro.media.xml_variant.codecs and ro.media.xml_variant.codecs_performance

measured_on_v15.camcorder_probe: CamcorderProfile.hasProfile/get and getAll by reflection from a root app_process on the phone: cameras 0 and 1 expose qualities 0-7 and 1000-1006 only, highest 1920x1080@30, no 2160p, 8K or high-speed quality
measured_on_v15.camera_application: In Video mode the Resolution (1080P) and Frame rate (30FPS) controls accept no tap, with Dolby Vision on or off; a long press opens only the control-rearrange panel
measured_on_v15.hal_metadata: Every rear device advertises 60 fps target ranges and 120/240 fps high-speed configurations, so the 1080p30 ceiling is the platform profile table, not the HAL

not_verified: the Xiaomi application's resolution and frame-rate controls after the property lands (its list may also depend on its own configuration)
4K, 8K and high-speed sessions on the camera HAL from this framework
Dolby Vision, stabilization and microphone behaviour at the new resolutions
other readers of the camcorder profile table (MediaRecorder clients such as Aperture)
